AI review is not clinical approval.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 1 (Claude)

answers.1: The head and upper neck of a person, seen from behind and slightly to the side. The face is turned away to the right, so only the edge of the nose, eye, eyebrow and the right ear are visible.
answers.2: One continuous drawing, no separate panels. On top of the head there is thick, dark brown hair, swept up and over toward the right. Below a sharp line that runs from the front hairline back over the ear and down toward the nape, the scalp is bare skin — a shaved-in undercut. Just under the parting line there is a band of very short stubble, drawn as fine dark flecks, which fades into completely smooth, pale skin over the back and side of the head, behind and below the ear, and down the neck. The ear is uncovered and looks normal. I see no rash, redness, scars, cuts, bumps, stitches, dressings, glasses, jewellery or anything applied to the skin.
answers.3: No text, numbers, arrows, labels, measurement lines or symbols anywhere in the picture. The background is plain off-white.
answers.4: A worried patient might read the bare area as hair loss — a large bald patch or shedding on the back and sides — rather than a deliberate haircut. It could also be mistaken for a pre-operation head shave.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 2 (Claude)

answers.1: A drawing of a person's head and upper neck, seen mostly from behind and slightly to the side, with the face turned to the right so only the edge of the eyebrow, eyelashes, nose tip and cheek show. The whole right ear, the side and back of the scalp, and the top of the neck are in view.
